model_answer:
## Bottom line

Netflix's global average revenue per paying membership (ARM) went from **$10.82/month in 2019 to $11.70/month in 2024** — up only **~8% (+$0.88)** over five years, a **~1.6% compound annual growth rate**. Over the same span, average paying memberships grew **~82%** and streaming revenue grew **~96%**. In other words, essentially *all* of Netflix's growth in this period came from adding members, not from monetizing each member more.

## Reported figures (from the 10-K "consolidated performance highlights")

| Year | Global ARM (monthly) | Y/Y change | Avg. paying memberships (M) | Streaming revenue ($B) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2019 | **$10.82** | +5% | 152.98 | $19.86 |
| 2020 | $10.91 | +1% | 189.08 | $24.76 |
| 2021 | $11.67 | +7% | 210.78 | $29.52 |
| 2022 | $11.76 | +1% | 222.92 | $31.47 |
| 2023 | $11.64 | (1%) | 240.89 | $33.64 |
| 2024 | **$11.70** | +1% (+4% F/X neutral) | 277.73 | $39.00 |

*Source: Netflix Form 10-K filings FY2019, FY2020, FY2021, FY2022, FY2023, FY2024 (SEC EDGAR). ARM = streaming revenue ÷ average paid memberships ÷ months in period, excluding sales taxes/VAT.*

## Regional ARM, 2019 vs. 2024

| Region | 2019 | 2024 | 5-yr change |
|---|---|---|---|
| US & Canada (UCAN) | $12.57 | $17.20 | **+37%** |
| EMEA | $10.33 | $10.96 | **+6%** |
| Latin America | $8.21 | $8.24 | **+0.4%** |
| Asia-Pacific | $9.24 | $7.29 | **–21%** |

## Why the global average barely moved while UCAN rose 37%

1. **Geographic mix shift.** Growth came overwhelmingly from lower-priced regions. UCAN fell from ~40% of paid memberships in 2019 (67.7M of 167.1M) to ~30% in 2024 (89.6M of 301.6M). APAC alone nearly quadrupled to 57.5M members at ~$7/month. Mathematically, adding low-ARM members dilutes the global average even as every region's own pricing rises.
2. **Foreign exchange.** Netflix discloses that roughly 55–57% of revenue is non-USD. The 2022 dollar surge and continued weakness in the Argentine peso, Japanese yen, and other currencies crushed reported ARM in APAC and LATAM. For FY2024, LATAM ARM was **–5% reported but +21% in constant currency**, and APAC **–5% reported vs. –3% F/X-neutral**; globally ARM was **+1% reported vs. +4% constant currency**. So reported ARM materially understates actual pricing power.
3. **Plan/pricing mix.** Netflix raised prices several times in UCAN and EMEA (and ended password sharing), but the cheaper ad-supported tier and mobile/low-price plans in emerging markets pulled the blended average down. Management explicitly cited plan mix and lower-ARM region growth as the reason ARM *fell* 1% in 2023.
4. **Definitional quirks worth knowing.** ARM divides *all* streaming revenue by *paid memberships*, so extra-member sub-account fees and (increasingly) advertising revenue flow into the numerator without adding members — a modest tailwind to ARM since 2023. It also excludes sales taxes/VAT, so it isn't the consumer's shelf price.
5. **Loss of disclosure.** Netflix stopped reporting quarterly memberships and ARM starting with Q1 2025 (it still gives regional revenue), so **FY2024 is the last full year of comparable ARM data** — which makes 2019–2024 the final clean multi-year ARM series.

**The takeaway for an investor:** Netflix's 2019–2024 story was volume, not price — member count did the heavy lifting (12.7% membership CAGR vs. 1.6% ARM CAGR). The strategic pivot in 2023–2025 (paid sharing, ad tier, price increases) is aimed at reversing that, and the F/X-neutral numbers (+4% in 2024) plus UCAN's +37% cumulative gain show that per-member monetization is accelerating beneath a flattish headline.
